title: Register Shifts and Rewriting
summary: Rewrite the same message for informal speech, neutral professional use, and formal writing.

sections.heading: Informal to neutral
sections.body: A strong C1 skill is recognizing informal features and replacing them without changing meaning. Common shifts include **tô → estou**, **pra → para**, **a gente → nós** or a verb-only form, and slang to neutral vocabulary.

examples.pt: Tô mandando o arquivo pra você.
Estou enviando o arquivo para você.
examples.en: I am sending you the file.

sections.heading: Neutral to formal
sections.body: Formal writing often uses more precise verbs, nominalizations, and explicit connectors, but should still be clear. Avoid making the sentence pompous.

examples.en: We are going to change the deadline.

sections.heading: Formal to plain language
sections.body: Advanced control also means simplifying bureaucratic Portuguese. Plain language is valued in many professional contexts.

examples.pt: Cumpre informar que o pagamento encontra-se pendente.
examples.en: It should be informed that payment is pending.

examples.pt: Informamos que o pagamento está pendente.
examples.en: We inform you that payment is pending.

examples.pt: O pagamento ainda não foi confirmado.
examples.en: Payment has not yet been confirmed.

keyPoints: Register shifts affect contractions, pronouns, vocabulary, and syntax.
Formal does not mean obscure or unnecessarily long.
Plain professional Portuguese can be both polite and clear.
Rewrite according to audience, medium, and purpose.

commonMistakes.wrong: Using slang in a formal complaint.
commonMistakes.right: Use neutral or formal vocabulary in official contexts.

commonMistakes.wrong: Replacing every verb with a nominalization.
commonMistakes.right: Use a mix of verbs and nouns for clarity.

commonMistakes.note: Do not mix registers and agreement patterns.
